title: Strengthening Weak Ties to the Organization
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses team members whose connection to the organization is thin and fading, arguing that remote work has made weak ties more common and more consequential. It insists leaders bear responsibility for actively rebuilding these connections rather than waiting for disengaged team members to reconnect on their own. Recommended tactics include more frequent check-ins and assigning disconnected team members to collaborative projects requiring interaction with multiple peers. The piece closes on the idea that frequent, substantive communication is the foundation of any strong relationship.
points: Weak ties to the organization are described as a growing retention risk, worsened by remote work.
Leaders bear responsibility for actively rebuilding connection rather than waiting on disengaged team members.
Increasing check-in frequency helps leaders understand what motivates a disconnected team member.
Assigning collaborative projects with multiple peers helps rebuild engagement more than solo work.
Frequent, substantive communication is framed as the foundation of any strong relationship.
quotes: Over time, team members without a strong connection to the organization will slowly disconnect and fade away.
The question is not why a weak tie exists, but rather how leaders can strengthen the connection and reengage the commitment of any team member who seems less connected than their peers.
The best leaders insist team members with weak ties contribute to assignments that require full engagement, in many cases with multiple colleagues.
It is nearly impossible for a team member to maintain a weak connection to the team if the leader doesn’t allow it.
Not surprisingly, increasing the connection any team member has with the team depends on more frequent and substantive communication.
